articles.title: Americans hate tipping. So why haven’t they stopped?
articles.summary: The backlash against tipping is loud. Restaurant gratuities are holding steady. What are diners really mad about?
articles.body:
I am a recovering people-pleaser, though I admit most of the recovering still takes place in private. I rehearse difficult conversations for weeks — on walks by the lake, in the shower, in the mirror — before actually having them. I've let subscriptions renew rather than endure the discomfort of calling to cancel. I once managed to pay extra for one of the worst haircuts of my life. And then there was the onyx. At a metaphysical shop, a cashier with impeccable black nails and at least six rings that looked like they had their own elaborate backstories silently turned a touchscreen toward me. It asked whether I'd like to leave a tip. Now, I'd never considered the etiquette of tipping for a rock, but something about the setting made pressing "No Tip" feel like tempting fate. I selected 15%, unwilling to risk the karmic consequences.

At an airport coffee shop, I'd retrieved a bottled juice from the refrigerator and selected a muffin , mummy-wrapped in plastic cling wrap. The cashier scanned my items, and the tablet swung around. Would I like to leave a tip? My suggested options were 20%, 23% and 25%.

For once in my life, I declined. The muffin, I reasoned, could hardly take it personally.

For all the complaints about tipping culture, however, Americans appear remarkably reluctant to abandon the practice where it's traditionally been expected. According to new data from restaurant technology company Toast , highlighted in an October 10 Food & Wine report , the average tip at full-service restaurants was 19.1% in the second quarter of 2026, while quick-service restaurants averaged 15.8%. Those figures, drawn from card and digital transactions that included gratuities, have barely budged over the last two years. Meanwhile, a 2025 Bankrate survey found that 63% of American adults held at least one negative view about tipping, including 41% who believed tipping culture had gotten out of control. Yet 70% of respondents who ate at sit-down restaurants said they always tipped their servers.

In other words, Americans have developed a fairly robust appetite for complaining about tipping, but considerably less enthusiasm for actually stopping.

The phenomenon has acquired its own name: " tipflation ." According to Google Trends, searches for the term were virtually nonexistent before November 2022, only to peak in popularity the following summer. The timing was hardly coincidental. Americans had spent much of the preceding year grappling with soaring prices on everything from groceries to gasoline. Now, just as they were adjusting to the fact that seemingly everything cost more, they were being asked to leave gratuities on transactions that had never previously seemed to require them.

Digital payment systems have made this negotiation both more ubiquitous and, somehow, more awkward. "The screen is just going to ask you a few questions," a cashier might say, employing a euphemism now familiar to anyone who has purchased a coffee in the last several years. What might once have been a couple dollars dropped into a jar has become an additional decision at checkout, complete with suggested percentages and the opportunity to feel vaguely terrible about selecting none of them.

Want more great food writing and recipes? Sign up for Salon's free food newsletter , The Bite.

And the irritation isn't entirely financial. The same screen might appear whether someone has prepared six elaborate espresso drinks or simply scanned a packaged muffin, leaving customers to make impromptu judgments about the value of someone else's labor. Is the employee earning a tipped wage? Does the gratuity go directly to them? These are rather complicated questions to consider while standing in line for coffee, particularly when the person behind you is waiting to order. What was once an opportunity to offer something extra has become a request customers must actively decline.

There is, however, an important distinction between resenting a tip request at an airport kiosk and deciding not to tip the person who has spent the last hour bringing you dinner. In most of the country, restaurant servers work under a compensation structure that explicitly assumes gratuities will make up a substantial portion of their earnings. Even where employers are required to pay the full minimum wage before tips, gratuities can remain an important part of a server's income.

Over time, this economic arrangement has also hardened into a remarkably durable social contract. Americans may disagree about whether to tip someone who pours an iced coffee from a jug, but at a full-service restaurant, the expectations are considerably clearer. The bill arrives, you calculate a gratuity and, assuming nothing has gone terribly wrong, you leave something in the neighborhood of 20%. For many diners, myself included, it's simply part of the cost of eating out, as much as the entrée or the glass of wine.

Of course, the trouble with calling tipping a social contract is that it makes it sound as though we all sat down and agreed on the terms. We didn't. The practice, imported from European aristocratic traditions, took hold in America after the Civil War , when white employers found in gratuities a convenient excuse to pay newly emancipated Black workers little or nothing. It became especially entrenched in the service industry, and when Franklin Roosevelt signed the Fair Labor Standards Act in 1938 , restaurant workers were among those excluded from its original minimum-wage protections. The federal tip credit, formally introduced in 1966, further institutionalized the notion that customers could be responsible for supplying a portion of workers' wages.

There's a reasonable argument, then, that this is a social contract overdue for renegotiation. But changing it requires more than convincing diners to stop leaving an extra $20 on the table. Restaurants operate on notoriously narrow margins, and even when price increases are necessary, customers don't always greet them enthusiastically.

During the recent egg-price spikes , I watched some of my favorite breakfast spots paste new prices over old ones, often with apologetic little notes explaining the change. That was just the cost of one ingredient; imagine trying to explain an entirely different system of paying the people who prepare and serve the meal.

Still, some restaurants have been experimenting with precisely that. In a 2022 interview with Salon's Maggie Hennessy , Ron Hsu, chef-owner of Atlanta's Lazy Betty , described his decision to move away from the traditional tipped-wage model in favor of paying employees at least the federal minimum wage and using service charges to distribute compensation more equitably between front- and back-of-house workers.

Interestingly, Hsu's restaurants were experimenting with different versions of that arrangement. At the higher-end Lazy Betty, the service charge was incorporated into menu prices; at the more casual (and now-closed) Juniper Cafe, customers saw an additional 20% on their bills. Hsu said the second approach met with more resistance, in part because staff were uncomfortable explaining the unfamiliar model to customers. Even when the money was ultimately going toward the same purpose, how it appeared on the bill mattered.

"One good thing Covid did is make everyone more aware of how difficult working in restaurants is," Hsu told Hennessy. "You can't work remotely if you're cooking or serving food. Because so many restaurants rely on face-to-face interaction to put forth their product, a lot of our customers were like, 'they're working during a pandemic. We're going out as entertainment, they're working to survive.' Everyone's awareness and empathy increased."

Still, he wasn't under any illusions about the difficulty of changing the system.

"Of course, there's still a lot of pushback. Not everyone that comes in likes it," he acknowledged.

"But it's gotta start somewhere. Danny Meyer tried implementing it in his restaurants [Union Square Hospitality Group] in New York in 2015, but it didn't work . I think we're decades away from truly seeing a different model. It is happening; we just have to do a little at a time and keep chipping away."

And perhaps that's what makes the online backlash against tipping more interesting than its angriest manifestations suggest. Consider r/EndTipping , a Reddit community whose name sounds like a call to arms against the gratuity line. Its stated mission, however, is to advocate for a system in which workers aren't dependent on tips, with labor costs folded into the prices customers see upfront. Members disagree about how to get there — including whether refusing to tip under the current system advances that goal or simply punishes workers — but the distinction matters.

Perhaps the more productive conversation isn't about whether Americans should tip more or less, but about how we build a hospitality industry in which workers are fairly compensated and diners understand what they're paying for. That will require experimentation, transparency and a willingness to accept that the true cost of a restaurant meal may look a little different than we're accustomed to.

In the meantime, refusing to tip your server isn't going to dismantle the system. It's just going to leave your server with less money.

But the next time a touchscreen asks you to leave a gratuity on a piece of onyx? Feel free to decline. I suspect the universe will understand.

articles.title: Germans to join Europe's youth protest wave
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of young Germans are set to demonstrate on Saturday, the latest in a wave of protests across Europe led by youths who complain political el...
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of young Germans are set to demonstrate on Saturday, the latest in a wave of protests across Europe led by youths who complain political elites are ignoring their concerns.

From France to Italy and Spain, young protesters have taken to the streets in recent weeks to make their voices heard, with demonstrations sometimes degenerating into serious violence.

In Germany, about 150,000 people have so far registered to turn out Saturday in around 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne, for protests led by a group dubbed "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!).

While the movement has stressed it rejects all violence, police are taking no chances and are deploying thousands of officers, while some luxury jewellery shops and clothing stores are boarding up their windows to ward off potential looters.

The protest movement has a range of complaints, from high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians deciding on policies with apparently little regard for the younger generation.

"We are young people who no longer want to sit back and watch while decisions are made about our future without us being heard," said a statement from the group, which describes itself as a non-partisan alliance.

"Wherever we look, we see crises and hardly any prospects for us."

Spending cuts are being made in areas ranging from education to culture and healthcare, they say.

"The cuts are being made at our expense, while big corporations continue to profit and billions flow into rearmament."

They are also unhappy with Germany's bid to boost its military through a new voluntary service model, and fear that mandatory conscription could be reintroduced.

Authorities are worried the protests, taking place on Halloween, could be marred by the same kind of violence seen elsewhere in Europe.

In France, nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerated into some of the country's worst rioting in years.

Berlin is in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests.

Marc Henrichmann, a senior lawmaker from the ruling centre-right CDU party, warned in an interview with the Handelsblatt newspaper that the "networking of the far-left extremist scene is international and coordinated".

But the interior ministry has stressed that a distinction must be drawn between "peaceful student protests" and a "violent extremist scene" that might hijack the demonstrations.

Authorities say that they do not as yet have any evidence of concrete plans for violence.

The "GenZ regelt!" movement meanwhile stressed that "extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us -- no matter from which side".

Christian Volk, an expert in protest movements, said there was the potential for Germany to see a major protest movement.

"There is an enormous amount of pressure building up," Volk, from Berlin's Humboldt University, told AFP.

Young people are demanding "that their political experiences and expectations for the future are also heard", he said.

But he said there were key differences with France, which has a "completely different tradition when it comes to confrontational forms of protest".

articles.title: Incêndio destrói lancha e deixa feridos na Praia de Toquinho; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Incêndio na embarcação aconteceu na manhã deste sábado (31). Vítimas foram três homens, que foram levados para hospital em Ipojuca, no Litoral Sul.
articles.summary: Embarcação pegou fogo enquanto estava atracada perto de um píer na manhã deste sábado (31). Vítimas foram socorridas e levadas para unidade de saúde em Ipojuca.
articles.body:
Uma lancha foi destruída pelo fogo após explodir na manhã deste sábado (31), na Praia de Toquinho, na cidade de Ipojuca , no Litoral Sul de Pernambuco ( veja vídeo acima ). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, três homens ficaram feridos no incêndio e foram socorridos .

Imagens enviadas ao g1 e à TV Globo mostram as chamas altas na embarcação, que estava atracada perto de um píer, onde também havia outros barcos. Não foi informado se as três vítimas estavam dentro da lancha no momento da explosão. Os nomes e as idades dos feridos não foram divulgados.

O Corpo de Bombeiros enviou duas viaturas ao local do incêndio e recebeu apoio do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), que também encaminhou duas viaturas.

"Ao chegar ao local, as equipes iniciaram o combate às chamas e realizaram o atendimento à ocorrência. Três vítimas foram socorridas e encaminhadas com vida a uma unidade hospitalar", afirmou o Corpo de Bombeiros em nota.

Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde das vítimas nem para qual hospital elas foram levadas. A Capitania dos Portos foi procurada pelo g1 , mas não enviou uma nota sobre o caso, até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Esse foi o segundo incêndio ocorrido na manhã deste sábado em praias de Pernambuco. O primeiro aconteceu na Praia de Ponta de Pedras, no município de Goiana, no Litoral Norte do estado, destruindo dois trailers num food park . Não houve feridos nesse caso.

articles.standfirst: Secretário de Estado afirmou que Donald Trump autorizaria a entrada do senador nos EUA caso ele chegasse a um ponto oficial de imigração.
articles.summary: Secretário de Estado afirmou que Donald Trump autorizaria a entrada do senador nos EUA caso ele chegasse a um ponto oficial de imigração.
articles.body:
O Secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio , disse neste sábado (31) que o governo norte-americano 'não se envolveu diretamente' na vinda de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ao país após a derrota nas urnas nas eleições brasileiras.

Flávio deixou o Brasil rumo aos EUA nesta semana, após ser derrotado nas eleições presidenciais e ter o passaporte incluído em um pedido de apreensão feito pelo ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Alexandre de Moraes.

“Não estávamos envolvidos em nenhum dos acordos ou preparativos que ele fez para deixar o país. Pelo menos, o governo dos Estados Unidos não participou diretamente de nenhuma das ações realizadas”, disse Rubio.

Além disso, o secretário de Estado também deixou claro que Donald Trump autorizaria a entrada de Flávio nos Estados Unidos, caso fosse necessário.

“O presidente deixou claro que, se ele chegasse aos Estados Unidos por um ponto de entrada, receberia autorização de entrada condicional (parole). E foi isso que aconteceu”, completou

Por fim, Rubio confirmou que deve se encontrar com o ministro de relações exteriores do Brasil, Mauro Vieira, durante o fórum do G7, na França.

Marco Rubio, Secretário de Estado dos EUA — Foto: AFP via Getty Images (BBC)

Assessor de Trump ajudou Flávio a fugir, diz imprensa norte-americana

O jornal americano “Wall Street Journal” foi o primeiro a publicou, na quarta-feira (28), a informação de que o assessor de comunicação da Casa Branca, Jason Miller, ajudou a conseguir o avião particular que transportou Flávio e a família na madrugada. Segundo o jornal, Santiago Caputo, um dos principais assessores do presidente argentino, Javier Milei, também fez parte do plano.

"Depois de cruzar a fronteira do Brasil com a Argentina, o carro de Flávio Bolsonaro foi escoltado pela Polícia de Segurança Aeroportuária da Argentina até o posto de controle de imigração do Aeroporto Internacional das Cataratas do Iguaçu. Santiago Caputo manteve contato direto com Eduardo Bolsonaro, irmão de Flávio, que mora nos Estados Unidos desde o ano passado, para coordenar a operação. No aeroporto, um jato particular da Baires Fly, empresa de voos fretados, aguardava a família”.

Jason Miller voltou a integrar a equipe da Casa Branca em setembro, de maneira temporária. Ele já tinha atuado como um dos principais assessores de Trump durante o primeiro mandato e as duas campanhas presidenciais. Chegou a visitar o Brasil em 2021 e se encontrou com o então presidente Jair Bolsonaro e o então deputado Eduardo.

articles.title: Feriado de Finados: veja o que abre e o que fecha no Amapá | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviços públicos, estabelecimentos comerciais e outros setores terão horário de funcionamento alterado, principalmente em Macapá e Santana. Veja o que muda.
articles.summary: Serviços públicos, estabelecimentos comerciais e outros setores terão horário de funcionamento alterado, principalmente em Macapá e Santana.
articles.body:
Veja o que muda no feriado de Finados — Foto: Fecomércio/Divulgação

Por conta do feriado de Finados, celebrado nesta segunda-feira (2), o funcionamento de serviços públicos, estabelecimentos comerciais e outros setores sofrerá alterações no Amapá . Os serviços considerados essenciais serão mantidos.

O g1 listou as principais alterações em Macapá e Santana . (veja abaixo)

Macapá e Santana : varejo de gêneros alimentícios (7h às 13h)

Lojas do centro comercial, calçados, móveis, eletrodomésticos, papelarias e representantes comerciais (8h às 13h)

Lojas de materiais de construção, elétricos e hidráulicos (8h às 15h)

Atacado de gêneros alimentícios (fechado)

As agências não abrirão. O funcionamento retorna ao normal na terça-feira (3). No dia de Finados, o atendimento eletrônico segue funcionando normalmente na Central 135 e pelo site e aplicativo Meu INSS.

Por ser um feriado nacional, as agências bancárias e lotéricas permanecerão fechadas. Com isso, os vencimentos de contas, incluindo boletos e de concessionárias, agendamento de pagamentos e envios de transferências foram prorrogados para o primeiro dia útil após a data.

Não haverá atendimento nas agências dos Correios.

Os órgãos públicos municipais e estaduais também não terão expediente durante o feriado. Apenas os serviços essenciais, como atendimentos de urgência e emergência em hospitais, Unidades Básicas de Saúde e UPAs, Samu, Segurança Pública, serão mantidos, conforme as escalas de plantão de cada órgão.

O Tribunal de Justiça do Amapá (Tjap), vai funcionar em regime de plantão durante o feriado. Atendimento presencial estará suspenso.

articles.title: Feriado de Finados: veja o que abre e o que fecha na região | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeituras terão mudanças no atendimento durante o feriado. São Carlos também tem feriado na quarta-feira (4).
articles.summary: Prefeituras terão mudanças no atendimento durante o feriado. Serviços essenciais, como os de saúde, serão mantidos para atender à população; confira.
articles.body:
Vista aérea de São Carlos, Rio Claro e Araraquara — Foto: Acervo EP

O Dia de Finados é celebrado nesta segunda-feira (2) e as prefeituras de Araraquara , São Carlos e Rio Claro (SP) terão alterações no funcionamento dos serviços públicos durante o feriado prolongado.

As agências bancárias de todo o país não terão atendimento presencial na segunda-feira (2), feriado de Finados. O atendimento será retomado na terça-feira (3), nas localidades sem feriado municipal.

Durante o feriado, os clientes poderão utilizar aplicativos, internet banking, caixas eletrônicos e correspondentes bancários. O Pix funcionará normalmente, 24 horas por dia. Contas de consumo com vencimento no dia 2 poderão ser pagas no próximo dia útil, sem acréscimo. Já tributos e impostos devem ser quitados antecipadamente para evitar juros e multas.

Para ajudar a população a se programar, o g1 São Carlos e Araraquara preparou um guia com o que abre e o que fecha nas três maiores cidades da região. Confira abaixo.

Igreja Santa Cruz de Araraquara, centro da cidade. — Foto: Amanda Rocha/g1

A Prefeitura de Araraquara terá alterações no atendimento ao público durante o feriado de Finados e o ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor Público. Os serviços administrativos serão suspensos a partir desta sexta-feira (30) e retomados na terça-feira (3), às 9h30.

Os serviços essenciais serão mantidos, com funcionamento ininterrupto das três Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPAs) do município.

UPA Central: Avenida Maria Antonia Camargo de Oliveira, na Vila Velosa. Atendimento 24 horas.

UPA Valle Verde: Rua Henrique João Baptista Crisci, s/nº, no Valle Verde. Atendimento 24 horas.

UPA Vila Xavier: Rua José do Patrocínio, 660, na Vila Santa Maria. Atendimento 24 horas.

Samu: atendimento 24 horas pelo telefone 192.

Casa de Acolhida: atendimento 24 horas pelo telefone (16) 3336-7510.

Postos de saúde e unidades da rede básica e especializada;

Centros de Referência de Assistência Social (Cras);

Coordenadoria de Vigilância em Saúde, incluindo as gerências de Vigilância Sanitária, Epidemiológica e Ambiental, Cerest e DST/Aids;

O Paço Municipal e os postos de atendimento da Prefeitura na Vila Xavier, no Selmi Dei e na Procuradoria Municipal voltam a atender na terça-feira (3), a partir das 9h30.

A cidade de São Carlos — Foto: Prefeitura/Divulgação

A Prefeitura de São Carlos divulgou o funcionamento dos serviços públicos municipais durante o feriado de Finados, na segunda-feira (2), o ponto facultativo de terça-feira (3) e o aniversário de 169 anos do município, na quarta-feira (4).

Os serviços essenciais, como atendimentos de urgência e emergência, serão mantidos. Algumas repartições públicas e unidades municipais terão o atendimento suspenso ou horários especiais.

Saúde: as UPAs da Vila Prado, Santa Felícia e Cidade Aracy funcionarão 24 horas. O Samu atenderá normalmente pelo telefone 192.

Farmácias municipais : na terça-feira (3), haverá plantão das 7h30 às 16h nas unidades das UBSs Botafogo e Delta e das USFs Itamaraty/São Rafael, Jockey/Guanabara e Zavaglia.

Farmácia de Alto Custo: atendimento na terça-feira (3), das 7h30 às 14h.

Farmácia da UPA Aracy: funcionará nos dias 31 de outubro e 1º, 2 e 4 de novembro, das 8h às 12h e das 13h às 18h, com dispensação de medicamentos para tratamentos agudos, conforme disponibilidade de estoque. Não haverá fornecimento de medicamentos de uso contínuo.

Serviços de água e esgoto (SAAE): emergências poderão ser comunicadas pelo telefone 0800-300-1520. O atendimento presencial será retomado na quinta-feira (5).

Ecopontos: funcionamento diário, das 8h às 12h.

articles.title: Fest Bossa & Jazz reúne público na primeira noite em Pipa | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival gratuito segue até domingo (1º), com shows de artistas nacionais, internacionais e potiguares em diferentes pontos da praia.
articles.summary: Festival gratuito começou nesta sexta-feira (30) na Praia da Pipa, em Tibau do Sul, com shows de Momô, Roberta Campos e outras atrações.
articles.body:
Fest Bossa & Jazz Pipa 2026 — Foto: Rogério Vital

A primeira noite do Fest Bossa & Jazz Pipa 2026 reuniu moradores e turistas na Praia da Pipa, em Tibau do Sul , nesta sexta-feira (30). Com entrada gratuita, o festival segue até domingo (1º), com apresentações de artistas nacionais, internacionais e potiguares em palcos espalhados pelo destino.

A programação começou com o cortejo da Bossa & Jazz Street Band, que percorreu as ruas de Pipa e convidou o público para os shows nos polos Pipa Atlântico e Praça do Pescador.

No Polo Pipa Atlântico, a cantora Momô abriu a sequência de apresentações com um repertório de jazz e blues. Em seguida, a artista Roberta Campos subiu ao palco e cantou músicas conhecidas do público, como "De Janeiro a Janeiro", "Minha Felicidade", "Casinha Branca", "Abrigo" e "Mundo Inteiro".

A turista paulista Ana Carla Sampaio elogiou a experiência de acompanhar os shows em Pipa. "Achei maravilhoso o show e, principalmente, esse local tão aconchegante que é o festival na rua aqui em Pipa. Está valendo muito a pena essa experiência. Amei!", afirmou.

No Polo Praça do Pescador, as apresentações ficaram por conta de Mago da Silva e da banda Prado Brothers. Nos intervalos dos shows, as DJs Carlota e Cris Flores animaram o público nos dois espaços.

Neste sábado (31), o festival segue com apresentações ao longo do dia e da noite. A programação completa pode ser consultada no perfil oficial do evento no Instagram, @festbossajazz, e no site festbossajazz.com.br.

O Fest Bossa & Jazz Pipa 2026 é realizado pela Juçara Figueiredo Produções, por meio do Programa Câmara Cascudo de Incentivo à Cultura, da Secretaria de Cultura do Governo do Rio Grande do Norte.

articles.title: Mulher é morta a facadas em frente a bar em Cariacica | G1
articles.standfirst: Priscila de Sales, de 39 anos, era cozinheira e mãe de quatro filhos. Segundo testemunhas, homem discutiu com a vítima, deixou o estabelecimento e voltou armado com uma faca. Polícia trata o caso como feminicídio.
articles.summary: Priscila de Sales, de 39 anos, era cozinheira e mãe de quatro filhos. Segundo testemunhas, homem discutiu com a vítima, deixou o estabelecimento e voltou armado com uma faca.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 39 anos foi morta a facadas em frente a um bar no bairro Alto da Boa Vista, em Cariacica, na Grande Vitória, na noite de sexta-feira (30). O suspeito, Leoni Martins Cabral, de 41 anos, se apresentou à polícia na manhã deste sábado (31) e foi autuado por feminicídio.

A vítima foi identificada como Priscila de Sales. Ela era moradora do bairro e frequentava o estabelecimento onde o crime aconteceu.

Segundo informações repassadas à polícia pela dona do bar, Priscila discutiu com um homem que também costumava frequentar o local. Depois da briga, ele foi embora, mas voltou armado com uma faca e atacou a mulher.

Testemunhas contaram que o suspeito morava a poucos metros do estabelecimento e fugiu depois do crime.

Mulher é morta a facadas em frente a bar em Cariacica e suspeito se entrega à polícia. Espírito Santo — Foto: TV Gazeta

Na manhã deste sábado, Leoni foi até a Delegacia Regional de Cariacica e se entregou. Ele foi levado por investigadores da Delegacia de Homicídios e Proteção à Pessoa (DHPP) para prestar depoimento.

Um parente da proprietária do bar, que preferiu não se identificar, contou que o suspeito era namorado da dona do estabelecimento.

Priscila era natural de Minas Gerais e morava havia pelo menos dez anos na Grande Vitória, segundo familiares. Ela trabalhava como cozinheira e tinha quatro filhos. O mais novo tem 9 anos.

De acordo com a polícia, o homem foi autuado por feminicídio e será encaminhado ao Centro de Triagem, localizado no Complexo Penitenciário Rodrigo Figueiredo da Rosa.

articles.title: Alemanha mobiliza polícia antes de protestos de jovens  | G1
articles.standfirst: Protestos são motivados pelo custo de vida, pela precariedade nas escolas e pelos cortes no orçamento; polícia mobilizou milhares de agentes diante do temor de saques e episódios de violência.
articles.summary: Protestos são motivados pelo custo de vida, pela precariedade nas escolas e pelos cortes no orçamento; polícia mobilizou milhares de agentes.
articles.body:
Manifestante segura cartaz durante protesto na Alemanha — Foto: Foto por INA FASSBENDER / AFP

A polícia alemã foi mobilizada neste sábado (31) em todo o país, enquanto muitos comerciantes protegiam suas vitrines e fachadas antes de manifestações que podem reunir dezenas de milhares de jovens.

Os organizadores do movimento "GenZ regelt!" ("A Geração Z dá conta do recado") esperam mais de 170 mil participantes em mais de 30 cidades , entre elas Berlim, Frankfurt e Colônia.

Os protestos são inspirados em movimentos semelhantes surgidos em outros países europeus, especialmente França e Itália, onde jovens manifestaram indignação contra elites políticas que acusam de ignorar suas preocupações .

Embora o movimento afirme rejeitar qualquer forma de violência, a polícia adotou medidas preventivas. Milhares de agentes foram mobilizados, e joalherias de luxo e lojas de roupas reforçaram a proteção diante do temor de possíveis saques.

As reivindicações incluem o aumento do custo de vida, a deterioração das condições nos estabelecimentos de ensino e os cortes orçamentários.

"A situação dos jovens é precária e, mesmo assim, eles continuam sem ser ouvidos", declarou Veronika Dinter, porta-voz do movimento.

Os manifestantes também criticam o forte aumento dos gastos militares e um novo programa de serviço voluntário destinado a reforçar as Forças Armadas, que, segundo eles, poderia abrir caminho para o restabelecimento do serviço militar obrigatório.

Também estão previstas grandes manifestações neste sábado na França. Os protestos de 17 de outubro resultaram em alguns dos mais graves distúrbios registrados no país nos últimos anos.

Manifestantes exibem cartazes com a frase “Taxem os ricos” durante ato organizado pelo movimento “GenZ regelt!”, na Alemanha. — Foto: Ina Fassbender/AFP

articles.title: Queimadas no Amazonas caem 39% em outubro, aponta Inpe | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado contabilizou 2.258 focos no mês, contra 3.726 em setembro. Apesar da redução, nove municípios apresentaram qualidade do ar de moderada a ruim nesta sexta-feira (31).
articles.summary: Queimadas no Amazonas caíram 39% em outubro, mas a fiscalização aplicou R$ 8,5 milhões em multas e nove cidades ainda sofrem com a má qualidade do ar.
articles.body:
Queimadas no Amazonas — Foto: Divulgação/Ibama

O Amazonas registrou 2.258 focos de queimadas em outubro , uma redução de 39,40% em relação a setembro, quando foram identificados 3.726 registros. Os dados são do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe).

Apesar da redução, o Amazonas ocupa a sexta posição entre os estados com mais focos de queimadas em 2026, com 8.515 registros. Entre quinta-feira (29) e sexta-feira (30), os satélites identificaram 30 novos focos em todo o território amazonense.

Apesar da queda no número de queimadas, a qualidade do ar continuou preocupante em parte do Amazonas. Na manhã deste sábado (31), nove municípios apresentaram índices de qualidade do ar que variaram de moderados a ruins, segundo o monitoramento do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva).

Em Iranduba e Parintins, a qualidade do ar chegou a variar entre ruim e muito ruim.

A redução no número de focos ocorre em meio às ações de fiscalização e combate a crimes ambientais no estado.

Entre os dias 9 e 28 de outubro, o Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas (Ipaam) aplicou R$ 8,5 milhões em multas e embargou 916,03 hectares durante a 13ª etapa da Operação Tamoiotatá 6.

As fiscalizações passaram por seis municípios: Borba , Careiro , Careiro da Várzea, Beruri , Manaquiri e Autazes . Entre as irregularidades identificadas estavam desmatamento sem autorização, queimadas ilegais, danos à vegetação nativa e descumprimento de embargos ambientais.

As ações ocorreram durante a vigência do Decreto Estadual nº 55.339, de 9 de setembro de 2026, que proíbe o uso do fogo no Amazonas por 120 dias.

articles.title: Jovem se surpreende ao ser 'atropelado' por boto em passeio de caiaque | G1
articles.standfirst: Lucas Ramponi estava gravando o passeio quando foi surpreendido pelo animal em Cananéia (SP).
articles.summary: Lucas Ramponi estava gravando o passeio quando foi surpreendido pelo animal em Cananéia (SP).
articles.body:
Lucas Ramponi de Almeida, de 32 anos, se surpreendeu ao ser "atropelado" por um boto-cinza enquanto remava com amigos no mar de Cananéia , no litoral de São Paulo. Ele estava gravando o passeio quando se deparou com o animal, que deu um salto muito próximo do caiaque (assista acima).

Ao g1 , Lucas revelou que está no mar quase diariamente, pois vende passeios de caiaque. Porém, nunca tinha vivido uma experiência tão próxima com os botos da região, como ocorreu nesta sexta-feira (30).

"Foi surreal. Ele subiu muito próximo. Acho que a hora que ele viu o caiaque, ele meio que me atropelou, né? Me deu um banho [...]. Foi realmente surpreendente", relembrou Lucas, que trabalha com turismo na cidade.

Jovem se surpreende ao ser 'atropelado' por boto em passeio de caiaque no litoral de SP — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com ele, a situação inusitada se tornou ainda mais inesquecível por ser gravada. "Fui gravar um vídeo aleatório", conta. Segundo ele, a recordação se tornou muito melhor do que esperava.

"Estou na água todos os dias, vejo [os botos] com frequência, mas fiquei impressionado [com a proximidade do animal] e por ter o privilégio de conseguir gravar, que é algo muito raro", ressaltou Lucas.

O jovem contou que a comunidade que pratica caiaque não procura se aproximar tanto dos animais como algumas pessoas que passeiam de barco.

"No caiaque, a gente tem uma visão totalmente diferente, porque é o boto que, por conta própria, chega e começa a acompanhar. Ele faz umas apresentações, acrobacias, surreais ao lado do caiaque", disse.

articles.title: Travessia Delfinópolis Cássia ganha balsa para 60 veículos | G1
articles.standfirst: Embarcação foi contratada em caráter emergencial pela Prefeitura de Delfinópolis para garantir a continuidade do transporte aquaviário durante reforma e manutenção de outras balsas.
articles.summary: A travessia Delfinópolis Cássia recebeu reforço emergencial de uma embarcação com capacidade para 60 veículos para suprir a manutenção de outras balsas no Rio Grande.
articles.body:
Uma nova balsa com capacidade para transportar até 60 veículos entrou em operação para reforçar a travessia do Rio Grande entre Delfinópolis e Cássia, no reservatório da Usina Hidrelétrica Mascarenhas de Moraes. A contratação emergencial foi oficializada pela Prefeitura de Delfinópolis com a empresa Navegação Confiança Ltda., por meio de um contrato de afretamento a casco nu.

O acordo foi firmado em 30 de outubro de 2026 e prevê investimento de R$ 880 mil pelo período de até 120 dias. O valor mensal do contrato é de R$ 220 mil.

Segundo a prefeitura, a medida tem como objetivo garantir mais segurança, conforto e eficiência no transporte de moradores, trabalhadores, produtores rurais e turistas que utilizam diariamente o serviço de travessia.

A nova embarcação é composta pela prancha CRB XV e pelo empurrador Comte Pietro. A contratação foi realizada para suprir a interrupção temporária das atividades da balsa São João Batista do Glória, que possui capacidade para 12 veículos e passará por reforma.

Nova balsa com capacidade para 60 veículos reforça travessia entre Delfinópolis e Cássia — Foto: Prefeitura de Delfinópolis

Além disso, a embarcação Rio Grande IV, que transporta até 18 veículos, também passará por manutenções, mas continuará operando durante o período.

Com a chegada da nova balsa, o sistema de travessia aquaviária passa a contar com três embarcações em operação: a balsa locada, com capacidade para até 60 veículos; a Balsa Canastra, com capacidade para até 33 veículos; e a Rio Grande IV, que transporta até 18 veículos. Já a Balsa São João Batista do Glória ficará temporariamente fora de operação para reforma.

O prefeito de Delfinópolis, Pedro Paulo Pinto, destacou que a locação estratégica tem como finalidade atender melhor a população e os visitantes que movimentam a região durante o feriado prolongado.

As operações de travessia ocorrem diariamente, incluindo fins de semana e feriados.

articles.title: Everton star reveals photo album capturing life behind the scenes
articles.summary: Merlin Röhl's camera lens takes fans inside the club's training ground for never-seen-before shots.
articles.body:
Premier League star Merlin Röhl has released a collection of pictures documenting behind-the-scenes moments during his time playing for Everton - two years after discovering a love for photography.

Called Behind the Lens: Life with Everton, the album captures the people, places and dramas that have shaped the German's introduction to life with the Toffees.

Asked what his favourite element of photography was, the 24-year-old said: "I think memories. I can hold on to something that normally just goes away.

"Sometimes it's just me doing something that I enjoy.

"I just enjoy playing football so much and I can't do it the whole day, so I'm trying next to the football to search for some things where I can feel a little bit like when I am playing football."

Everton signed the Germany under-21 international from Bundesliga side Freiburg on a season-long loan in 2025 before signing him permanently over summer.

The 6ft 3in midfielder joined Freiburg from Ingolstadt in 2022 and made 60 appearances, playing in several roles in midfield as well as deputising at right-back.

The footballer said photography provided an outlet for him to relax away from the pitch.

"I had a tough training session in the morning and did all the work that I can do on the pitch and sometimes for me it's to relax, to just go out, walk a little bit and have some photos," he said.

Röhl's camera takes supporters inside Everton's Finch Farm training ground and the club's dressing room, through recovery sessions and quiet moments around training.

It also chronicles journeys with teammates and into the build-up to matchdays home and away.

Away from football, his photographs explore Liverpool through walks around the city's parks, beaches, and the streets and spaces that have helped make Merseyside feel increasingly like home to him.

Some the proceeds of the book will support the Everton Multi Academy Trust, which is supported directly by Everton Football Club and Everton in the Community.

While it took some of Röhl's teammates a little while to warm up to the camera, now they have become comfortable in front of the lens.

"I think in the beginning it was a little bit kind of a step we needed to overcome, but now everybody is just like completely fine," he said.

"I have a good relationship with all my teammates and that helps a lot to get some nice pictures."

However, a certain key member of staff is yet to pose for Röhl's - his manager David Moyes.

"Maybe I will ask in the future," he said.

"But maybe I'm a little bit scared to affect my starting position."

articles.title: Tinder killer who believed he was a warlock said he 'picked the wrong person' after murdering woman
articles.summary: Sydney Loofe's friend catfished her killer's girlfriend on Tinder, providing the first major break in the Nebraska murder investigation.
articles.body: Sydney Loofe thought she was heading out for a second date with a woman she met on Tinder. Instead, the 24-year-old vanished — and the man convicted of her murder would later make a disturbing admission about why she proved to be the "wrong person" to kill. "I don't regret killing Sydney," Aubrey Trail said, according to filmmaker Christopher St. John. "I don't regret killing somebody, but I regret killing ... I picked the wrong person." Trail, then a 52-year-old con man, was convicted of strangling the Nebraska store clerk with an electrical cord in 2017, cutting her body into 14 pieces, placing the remains in garbage bags and dumping them in roadside ditches. At the trial, witnesses testified that Trail and his girlfriend, Bailey Boswell, then 25, had solicited them for group sex and talked about the occult and gaining "powers" through killing. ARIZONA MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WOMAN AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA FIRST DATE ENDS IN DESERT GRAVE "One of the FBI agents said that the culprits were in a frenzy," St. John told Fox News Digital. "They were looking to do this, and Sydney was the available target. She was trusting and innocent and fit the profile. You then later hear Aubrey Trail, the murderer, says, 'I picked the wrong person.'" "I think that's incredibly chilling for me because he has no remorse, but he wishes that he hadn't chosen someone with such strong family and friends because it led to his capture." Loofe's murder at the hands of Trail, who described himself as a "powerful warlock" and the leader of a sex cult, is explored in the new Hulu true crime docuseries "Swipe Right on the Devil." The three-part series features interviews with Loofe's loved ones and investigators, as well as recordings of Trail from death row. Loofe, a cashier at Menards, a home improvement store, lived alone in an apartment with her cat, Mimsy. According to friends, she was yearning for a relationship. On Tinder, she came across a profile for a woman named Audrey, an alias used by Boswell. After matching and exchanging messages, the two women went on their first date. They planned a second date for the next day. Loofe was smitten. "Sydney was like any one of us," said St. John. "She was feeling lonely and searching for belonging. She had gone on a date with this woman, and she was so excited that she immediately wrote to her friends. They were like, 'Great, nothing to worry about.' And she was never heard from again. Something awful came out of the darkness." When Loofe didn't show up for her morning shift the following day, her family requested a welfare check. Police found her car in the driveway. Her work clothes and purse were laid out for work. Her cat hadn't been fed. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Loofe's friend, Brooklyn McCrystal, knew that she had been on a date the night before she disappeared. McCrystal created a Tinder profile to find Audrey in hopes of getting her contact information. When McCrystal matched with Audrey on the dating app, they exchanged phone numbers. McCrystal gave Boswell's information to police. Loofe's friends also showed investigators her final social media post, a selfie shared on Snapchat captioned "Ready for my date." "Brooklyn provided the first big break in the case," said St. John. "She catfished the bad guys. There's digital tracking. It's got all the hallmarks of an amazing investigation. But ultimately, what led to Aubrey and Bailey's capture was the people who were devoted to Sydney searching for answers." Boswell refused to cooperate with investigators. When police tracked her phone, they learned it was a burner phone registered under a fake name. They traced the phone to hotels in the area, where surveillance video and a state-issued ID presented at check-in helped investigators identify Boswell as "Audrey." The video also showed that she was traveling with an older man, Trail. The Lincoln Journal Star reported that Loofe's phone last pinged at Boswell and Trail's apartment that night. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the apartment, which smelled strongly of bleach. Boswell and Trail had paid their rent early and left. Police named Boswell and Trail as persons of interest. On Nov. 29, 2017, the couple released a video on social media denying any involvement in Loofe's disappearance. Boswell said she had gone on two dates with Loofe, but after their second date, she had dropped Loofe off at a friend’s house. Despite maintaining their innocence, they went on the run. Boswell and Trail were arrested on Nov. 30, 2017, near Branson, Missouri, on unrelated federal fraud charges. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Nearly three weeks after Loofe disappeared, investigators used cellphone data to trace Boswell and Trail's movements and identify rural areas where they appeared to have slowed down or stopped. On Dec. 4, 2017, investigators searched a roadside ditch near Edgar, Nebraska. They found car keys, a phone, a label with Loofe's name and her dismembered upper arm, which bore a tattoo that read "Everything will be wonderful someday." The Lincoln Journal Star reported that some garbage bags contained her clothing. According to court documents, Trail and Boswell were captured on surveillance video at a Home Depot in Lincoln on Nov. 15, 2017, buying tools investigators believed were used to dismember Loofe, hours before her death. Investigators believed Boswell and Trail had lured Loofe through Tinder before killing her and dismembering her body. articles.title: Motorcyclist dies after falling into sea in Great Orme crash
articles.summary: The man was recovered from the water and airlifted to hospital but was pronounced dead, police say.
articles.body:
A man has died after falling into the sea following a crash involving his motorbike, police have said.

Officers from North Wales Police were called to reports of a crash involving a black motorcycle on Marine Drive on the Great Orme in Llandudno, Conwy county, at about 22:31 GMT on Thursday.

A multi-agency response including police, the RNLI and HM Coastguard was launched and the man was recovered from the water and airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor, where he was pronounced dead.

Police are looking to speak to the driver of a black vehicle - possibly a Ford Fiesta - that they believe was in the area at the time.

The incident happened about one mile (1.6km) from the Toll House towards the direction of the Great Orme summit.

The Great Orme is a headland which rises up to 207m (679 feet) above sea level and has sheer cliffs.

The man's kin have been informed and the coroner has been notified, police said.

Sgt Alun Jones said the force's thoughts were "with the man's family and friends at this very difficult time".

A force spokesperson said the black vehicle "travelled on Mostyn Street into North Parade then headed up towards the Great Orme at around 22:26".

"We are urging the driver of that vehicle to come forward as soon as possible," they said.

Police have appealed for anyone with information or video footage to contact them and they are particularly keen to hear from anyone travelling from the Toll House towards the Great Orme summit between 22:00 and 22:30 on Thursday and who may have dashcam footage.

The Great Orme is a limestone headland on the north coast of Wales, rising up to 207m (679 feet) above sea level.

It features sheer cliffs that drop dramatically straight into the Irish Sea.

It is a tourist attraction, with a Victorian tramway, a cableway, walking routes and a mining museum.

Llandudno's Marine Drive, the site of the crash, is a five-mile (8km) toll road looping around the base of the Great Orme.

articles.title: Meet Merlin, the 180-pound US pet pig who uses 25 buttons to demand food, call his owners and express anger, earning a Guinness World Records title and millions of online fans
articles.summary: A 180-pound pet pig in California has found an unusual way to make his wishes known, using 25 sound buttons to communicate with his owners.
articles.body: A 180-pound pet pig in California has found an unusual way to make his wishes known, using 25 sound buttons to communicate with his owners. Merlin can request food, ask to go outside, call his family and even express frustration when things do not go his way. His owner, Mina Alali, began training him when he was just 2.5 months old, gradually introducing buttons linked to everyday words and commands. Four years later, the pig has become a social media attraction, with videos of his interactions drawing millions of views and his Instagram account earning a Guinness World Records title.How Merlin uses 25 buttons to communicate with his familyMerlin's communication system is built around a set of 25 buttons placed on the floor of his family's home. Each one plays a particular word or expression, allowing him to signal what he wants without making a sound himself. The vocabulary includes simple responses such as yes and no, requests for food and phrases connected to his feelings.Some of the buttons are used to call his owners, Mina Alali and her fiancé, whom Merlin refers to as Mommy and Daddy. Others allow him to ask for playtime or indicate that he wants to go outside. The system has become part of his everyday routine, with Mina sharing recordings of his interactions online.Merlin can request vegetables and ask for snacks, sometimes shortly after finishing a meal. His owners have also recorded moments when he becomes frustrated after being refused something he wants. In those situations, his behaviour can include shouting and slamming doors.Mina Alali began training Merlin when he was just 2.5 months oldMerlin joined Mina's household in March 2022, fulfilling her long-standing wish to own a pig. The early months required considerable adjustment. He was vocal, frequently squealed and had not yet learned the behaviour expected of a household pet.Mina started introducing commands when he was around 2.5 months old. Over the following four years, she developed his ability to respond to different sounds and use the buttons. Guinness World Records reported that the training relied heavily on patience and positive reinforcement, with food serving as a particularly effective reward.Pigs are highly motivated by food, which made treats useful during the process. Mina also found that Merlin could become stubborn when something did not go his way. She has compared some of his reactions to those of a young child, particularly when he becomes impatient or frustrated.Before adopting Merlin, Mina had attracted attention online by teaching her bearded dragon, Mochi, to follow commands commonly associated with dogs. Videos showing the reptile responding to instructions such as come, wait and high five helped her build an audience of more than a million TikTok followers.The pig became an Instagram record holder with 1.1 million followersMerlin's button-based communication gradually became the focus of Mina's social media accounts. Videos showing him asking for food, calling his owners and reacting to everyday situations attracted viewers interested in his unusual behaviour. By March 2026, his Instagram account had accumulated approximately 1.1 million followers. Guinness World Records recognised him as the pig with the most followers on Instagram, giving him a record title that extended his popularity beyond social media.Mina told Guinness World Records that people increasingly recognised Merlin when they took him out. She and her fiancé have joked that walking him through public places feels like being accompanied by a major celebrity. His online presence has also brought attention to the way pigs interact with people. Mina has said she wants viewers to recognise that pigs have emotional and intellectual abilities that are sometimes overlooked when they are regarded primarily as livestock.Merlin behaves like a household pet despite weighing 180 poundsAlthough he is considerably larger than many people might expect from a pet described as a mini pig, Merlin shares several habits with domestic dogs. He is trained to walk on a lead and regularly accompanies his owners on trips around town. He also enjoys spending time indoors, particularly in the air-conditioned California home.His routine includes breakfast and dinner, with fresh fruit and vegetables used as treats during training. When he wants to go outside, he can press the corresponding button. Merlin also lives alongside several other animals. His household includes a dog, a pigeon, another bearded dragon and three rats. His buttons give him a way to request attention from his owners or signal that he wants to interact with his animal companions.Mina has described how Merlin sometimes gets himself trapped in the laundry room after becoming annoyed. The family may hear the door stopper make a noise before discovering where he has gone. He has a button for saying that he is mad, although his owners do not always need it to understand his mood.Why Mina says keeping a mini pig requires more than trainingMerlin's popularity has also given Mina an opportunity to discuss the responsibilities involved in keeping pigs as pets. Merlin weighs around 180 pounds, or 82 kilograms, illustrating how much larger these animals can become than prospective owners might anticipate.Mina has pointed out that some pigs are eventually rehomed because their owners were not prepared for their adult size. Many people expect them to remain below 100 pounds, even though weights above that are common. Merlin's training eventually helped him pass an assessment to become a certified therapy pig through the American Mini Pig Association, according to the Guinness World Records.From a talking pig to a different understanding of animal behaviourFor Mina, Merlin's popularity is closely connected to her interest in demonstrating what pigs can learn and how they express themselves. She has described him as an animal with a broad range of emotional responses, including happiness, frustration, anger and confusion. The buttons do not mean Merlin speaks in the same way as a human. They provide a method of associating particular sounds with actions, requests and situations. His ability to use them has developed through repeated training and interaction with his family.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh Congress president YS Sharmila has shifted her daughter's wedding to another venue after her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh Congress president YS Sharmila has shifted her daughter's wedding to another venue after her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, refused to allow his Bengaluru property to be used for the ceremony.In a social media post on X, Sharmila defended her ownership claim over the Yelahanka property and said it was allotted entirely to her and her children as part of the division of family assets after her brother Jagan Reddy became chief minister.“What is mine is mine, but the greed to covet it is not in my nature. After Jagan Mohan Reddy became chief minister, the Yelahanka property, which until then was a joint family property, came entirely (100 per cent) to my share and that of my children as part of the division of assets. This is the truth, with God as my witness," Sharmila said."Since it is my children's right and the house where my father YSR lived, we wanted to hold my daughter Anjili's wedding there, as she had wished. Ask any household in Telugu society, and they will tell you that getting one's daughter married in one's own house is considered a blessing for every parent," she added.Sharmila said she had decided to organise her daughter's wedding ceremony elsewhere as it was her responsibility to ensure that the event remained free of controversy."However, we are very saddened that we could not fulfil my daughter's wish to have her wedding at the very house where she grew up. My salutations to everyone who felt concerned about my daughter after seeing the developments taking place over the wedding venue," she said."My daughter Anjili's marriage is a match arranged by elders. It is our responsibility to conduct the wedding without controversy and without any disputes. Therefore, we have decided to hold the wedding ceremony of YS Anjili Reddy and Somala Raghuram Reddy at a different venue instead of the Yelahanka house, in the presence of relatives, friends and well-wishers. We wholeheartedly wish that the Telugu people will shower their blessings and good wishes on the couple,” she added.This comes after Jagan Mohan Reddy cited security reasons for refusing to let out the Yelahanka Palace for the wedding ceremony of his niece, Anjili Reddy, in Bengaluru.In the letter, he pointed out that a wedding would bring a large number of guests, caterers, decorators, photographers and other service providers into the residential premises."At the end of the day, this is my home and I want to ensure that my family and I are safe here," Jagan wrote.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 82% disapprove of Trump. So why are fewer Indian-Americans identifying as Democrats?
articles.summary: Explore the paradox of Indian Americans' political inclinations as 82% disapprove of Trump yet fewer identify as Democrats, highlighting changing allegiances and concerns within the community.
articles.body: At an Indian restaurant in Irving, near Dallas, Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico tried his hand at making a masala dosa, spreading batter on a hot pan and filling it with spiced potatoes. In Connecticut, Governor Ned Lamont joined Diwali celebrations, while Republican Congressman John James visited a Swaminarayan temple in Michigan. From dosas to Diwali and temple visits, politicians from both parties are making symbolic overtures to Indian-American voters ahead of the November 3 midterms. But the community’s political allegiances are not as straightforward as those campaign gestures might suggest.At the national level, Republicans are fighting hard to retain control of both chambers of Congress. And the odds, at least in prediction markets, are not in their favour. As of October 30, betting website Kalshi gave Democrats a 92% chance of taking control of the House of Representatives and a 69% chance of winning the Senate. Polymarket's corresponding figures were 94% and 72%.A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on October 26 also found Democrats leading Republicans 47% to 36% among registered voters. Losing control of either chamber, or in the worst case both, could severely hamper US President Donald Trump's legislative agenda in the final two years of his presidency. So the stakes couldn't be higher.With the Trump administration pursuing what many see as anti-immigration policies, the stakes are also fairly high for the 5.2 million people of Indian origin living in the US. However, there is an interesting paradox between their voting patterns and declared political affiliations. While most are strongly anti-Trump, many don't identify as Democrats. The party's perceived leftward tilt appears to be one source of discomfort among some Indian-Americans.An AP-NORC and AAPI Data survey released on October 19 found that 82% of Indian-American respondents disapprove of Trump's job performance. Yet four in ten held an unfavourable opinion of the Democrats. A separate series of surveys by the Carnegie Endowment earlier in the year suggests that fewer Indian-Americans identify as Democrats than they did six years ago, while more describe themselves as independents.Together, the surveys challenge the idea of Indian-Americans as a politically uniform community. They reveal differences across age, education, income and other factors that shape political affiliation.A clear Democratic leadThe AP-NORC/AAPI Data survey, conducted from September 8 to 15, found Trump's handling of the economy similarly unpopular: 81% disapproved and 18% approved. On immigration, 70% disapproved of his performance.Almost in lockstep, the Republican Party was viewed favourably by only 19%, while 70% held an unfavourable opinion of it. Democrats were in a substantially stronger position, with 51% viewing the party favourably.That advantage also appears in surveys measuring voting intentions. The 2026 AAPI Voter Survey, conducted by AAPI Data and APIAVote between June and July, found that 66% of Indian-American registered voters preferred Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives, against 18% favouring Republicans. Democratic Senate candidates also attracted 66%, compared with 22% for Republicans.Fewer are calling themselves DemocratsAccording to the Carnegie Endowment's 2026 Indian-American Attitudes Survey, conducted between November 2025 and January 2026, the share of Indian-American adults identifying as Democrats declined from 52% in 2020 to 48% in 2024 and 46% in 2026. Over the same period, Republican identification rose from 15% to 19%, while independent identification increased from 23% to 29%.Republicans' gains came between 2020 and 2024; between 2024 and 2026, their share of party identifiers remained unchanged at 19%. The independent share, meanwhile, rose four percentage points. The two-point dip in Democratic identification during this period is small relative to the survey's margin of error.Being independent, however, does not mean being undecided, particularly given the two-party nature of US politics. Carnegie found that the independent share dropped from 29% to 17% when respondents were offered the option of leaning towards one of the two parties.The ideological picture offers another clue. Carnegie found that 32% of Indian-Americans identified as moderates in 2026, up from 28% in 2024. The share selecting the specific label 'liberal' declined from 25% to 21%. But when those identifying as slightly liberal and extremely liberal are included, the broader liberal segment has changed little over the past six years. Rather than indicating a conservative shift, Carnegie describes the community as broadly centrist, with a left-of-centre tilt.On a scale of zero to 100, the Democratic Party's average rating in Carnegie's survey fell from 60 in 2024 to 53 in 2026. The Republican Party's rating also dropped, from 41 to 34. The decline extended to leading political figures. Kamala Harris's average rating fell from 62 to 52, while Trump's dropped from 40 to 32.Exhausted, but engagedThere is another striking finding from the AAPI Voter Survey. Although 92% of Indian-American registered voters said they planned to vote in November, 66% said they always (29%) or often (37%) felt exhausted when thinking about politics.At the same time, 43% described themselves as more enthusiastic than usual about voting in the midterms, compared with 22% who were less enthusiastic, perhaps because a lot more is at stake now.Three-quarters of respondents said they had discussed politics with family or friends in the previous year. Another 25% had discussed politics or community issues through group messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, while 24% had posted about politics on social media.But direct party outreach tells a different story. Forty percent of Indian-American registered voters reported receiving no contact from the Democratic Party over the preceding year, while 56% said the same of Republicans.The Democratic drift is not uniformCarnegie's findings also challenge the idea that younger Indian-Americans are necessarily moving away from Democrats. Among respondents aged 18 to 29, Democratic identification increased from 51% in 2024 to 56% in 2026. Among those aged 50 and above, however, it declined from 47% to 39%.Education produced another divide. Democratic identification among respondents without a college degree fell from 48% to 35%, while remaining broadly unchanged among college graduates, at 49%. Income revealed a similar split. Among Indian-Americans in households earning between $50,000 and $99,999 annually, Democratic identification declined from 54% to 44%. Among those in households earning at least $100,000, it increased from 46% to 51%.Gender differences were also visible. Democratic identification among men fell from 46% to 40%, while among women it rose slightly, from 50% to 52%. So older Indian-Americans appear to be moving away from identifying as card-carrying Democrats, although the trend among the well-off is different.Economy remains the big issueIn the September AP-NORC/AAPI Data poll, 87% of Indian-American respondents identified the economy as one of the most important election issues. Cost of living followed at 84%, while 76% said the same of healthcare.Despite weaker party identification, Democrats enjoyed sizeable advantages on these issues. Fifty-three percent trusted Democrats more to handle the economy, compared with 12% who trusted Republicans. On the cost of living, the corresponding figures were 52% and 8%. On healthcare, Democrats held an even larger advantage, with 60% trusting them more, against just 6% for Republicans.But these preferences did not amount to universal confidence in the party. On the economy, 20% trusted neither party. On the cost of living, the proportion was 25%.Democrats also had an advantage on immigration in the September survey, with 50% trusting them more, against 18% who preferred Republicans. On crime, however, the numerical gap was narrower: 29% trusted Democrats more and 19% Republicans, while 28% trusted neither.India ties not a major concernInflation and prices were the single most important policy issue for 21% of respondents in Carnegie's survey, followed by jobs and the economy at 17%. Healthcare ranked next at 13%, followed by immigration at 11%. Only 2% named US–India relations as their top concern.That is perhaps along expected lines, though many in India probably view Indian-Americans' political behaviour through the prism of the India–US bilateral relationship. For most desis living in the US, it is not the top concern.The finding does not mean that Indian-Americans are indifferent to relations between Washington and New Delhi. It means that domestic issues, particularly economic concerns, matter more when respondents are asked to identify their single most important policy priority.Is the Democratic Party's leftward tilt a problem?Carnegie asked respondents who did not identify as Democrats to rank their top two objections to the party. The most frequently cited reason, at 19%, was the perception that Democrats were too influenced by their left wing.Concerns about the party's approach to illegal immigration and disagreements with its economic policies followed at 17% each. Another 16% cited perceptions that Democrats were too soft on crime, while an equal share objected to what they considered excessive emphasis on identity politics. These issues overlap with broader conservative criticism of what is often called liberal or 'woke' politics. The findings suggest that the Democratic Party's perceived leftward tilt makes it harder for some Indian-Americans to identify with the party.But there is another side to this argument.The same Carnegie survey found that 68% of Indian-Americans who were familiar with Zohran Mamdani were enthusiastic about his election as New York City mayor, while 22% were unenthusiastic. Among those enthusiastic about his victory, 44% cited the expectation that he would govern as a liberal or progressive. Among those unenthusiastic, 36% said he was too liberal or progressive. Even among Indian-Americans identifying as Republicans, enthusiasm and opposition to Mamdani's victory were almost evenly divided, at 44% and 45%, respectively.That makes the political picture more complicated. Some Indian-Americans regard the Democratic Party as too influenced by its left wing, while others welcome the rise of progressive politicians such as Mamdani.The question beyond November 3There are important limitations to these findings. The relatively small ethnic subgroups surveyed carry greater statistical uncertainty than the surveys' overall samples. Carnegie's historical survey waves also involved different respondents and changes in sampling methods, so the reported shifts do not establish that individual voters have switched party allegiance.What the surveys do show is a distinction between candidate preference and party identity. Democratic candidates continue to enjoy a large advantage. Trump's job performance is viewed negatively by a substantial majority. Beyond the midterms, the challenge for Democrats will be to sustain their electoral support among Indian-Americans while addressing the concerns of those who no longer identify strongly with the party.Attention will eventually turn to the nomination contests ahead of the 2028 presidential election. The continuing influence of the MAGA movement within the Republican Party, and the ideological direction of the Democrats, will be among the factors shaping the political choices facing Indian-Americans. For now, though, the polling suggests that many desis would like to give Trump the electoral blues.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Heirs of Jewish banker have sued Sotheby’s over £1.2m painting sale, claiming artwork was looted by Nazis during World War II; a Parisian court to soon give ruling
articles.summary: A painting by French Impressionist Camille Pissarro, sold by Sotheby’s for £1.2 million in 2024, has become the centre of a legal battle involving the
articles.body: A painting by French Impressionist Camille Pissarro, sold by Sotheby’s for £1.2 million in 2024, has become the centre of a legal battle involving the heirs of a Jewish banker whose art collection was seized by the Nazis during World War II. Seven descendants of Salomon Flavian have approached a Paris court seeking to overturn the agreement that allowed the painting to be sold, arguing that most of the family was not consulted before the settlement was reached. The auction house disputes the claim that the artwork was looted and has also challenged the French court’s jurisdiction.According to The Art Newspaper, which reported on the proceedings in September 2026, the dispute concerns 'Darse de pêche et bassin Duquesne, Dieppe, après-midi ensoleillée', a 1902 painting depicting the French port town of Dieppe. Sotheby’s sold the work in London on June 25, 2024, for £1.2 million, below its estimated price range of £1.5 million to £2.5 million. The Paris court is expected to deliver its ruling on November 5, 2026.Painting’s disputed journey through historyPissarro’s painting was owned by Flavian, a Jewish banker and art collector who lived in Paris during the 1930s. His extensive art collection was seized by the Nazis in 1941, and his descendants believe the Dieppe painting was among the works taken. The painting’s history has attracted scrutiny because it appears in France’s postwar Répertoire des biens spoliés, a government register of property reported as looted during the German occupation. The register was published between 1947 and 1949 to help identify and recover property that had not yet been returned to its owners.However, the presence of an artwork in the register does not, by itself, conclusively establish every detail of how it changed hands. The painting’s wartime provenance, or documented history of ownership, is now at the heart of the legal dispute. Sotheby’s catalogue acknowledged Flavian’s ownership and the painting’s inclusion in the register. It also stated that the work was being offered for sale pursuant to a settlement between its current owner and Flavian’s heirs.The painting subsequently appeared in exhibitions at major art institutions, including Tate in London, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the Philadelphia Museum of Art, according to reports on the case.Seven heirs challenge settlementThe legal challenge is not limited to whether the painting was stolen. It also concerns how the settlement was negotiated and whether all the heirs were properly represented. According to The Art Newspaper, seven family members told the Paris court during a September 18 hearing that only two relatives, Gilles and Nicolas Flavian, had signed the agreement. They argue that the other descendants were not consulted before the deal was finalised.Under the arrangement, the two signatories waived their rights to the painting in connection with the sale. Four months after the auction, other family members reportedly received a letter from Mondex Corporation, a Toronto-based firm specialising in recovering assets lost during the Holocaust. The letter said an 8% share of the net sale price had been accepted on their behalf in exchange for their cooperation. An accompanying account statement referred to a 16% commission associated with the two heirs who signed the agreement.The seven plaintiffs are seeking to have the settlement annulled, arguing that they were excluded from decisions affecting their family’s claim to the artwork. Sotheby’s maintains that the settlement was disclosed in its catalogue. In a statement reported by The Jewish Chronicle, the auction house said: “Those discussions resulted in a settlement agreement between the consignor and Mondex, which was fully disclosed in our catalogue and pursuant to which the work was sold.”Was the painting actually looted?The painting’s wartime history remains contested. Sotheby’s and Mondex have relied on provenance research commissioned by the sellers, which concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that the work had been seized by the Nazis.The research, conducted by scholar Mary Kate Cleary, found no reference to the painting in the confiscation lists maintained by the Nazi task force known as the Einsatzstab Reichsleiter Rosenberg, which was responsible for looting artworks during the war.The research suggested that the painting may instead have been sold by Paris art dealer Paul Rosenberg to British collector Edward Le Bas around 1938, before the Nazi occupation of France. References to Le Bas in historical records were cited in support of this interpretation.The heirs’ lawyer, Corinne Hershkovitch, challenged that conclusion. She argued that the absence of the painting from the Nazi inventories did not necessarily prove that it had not been looted. She also questioned whether the historical records used in the research had been interpreted correctly and argued that additional family archives could help clarify the painting’s ownership.Mondex’s lawyer, Melina Wolman, maintained that the firm believed the painting had been wrongly registered as looted. Mondex founder James Palmer said the firm had adopted its position after examining the available evidence. The competing accounts mean that the question of whether the painting was forcibly taken from Flavian’s collection remains unresolved.Sotheby’s questions French court’s authorityThe auction house has also argued that the Paris court lacks jurisdiction because the transaction took place in London between parties it says had no direct relationship with France. The heirs’ case, however, is rooted in the painting’s alleged seizure in Paris during the Nazi occupation and the subsequent dispute over the rights of Flavian’s descendants.The court’s decision could therefore determine not only whether the settlement can be challenged, but also how the family’s claims will proceed. The ruling is not necessarily a final determination of the painting’s wartime history or ownership. The case highlights the difficulties that can arise decades after the Holocaust, when artworks have passed through multiple owners, historical records are incomplete and descendants seek to recover property taken from their families.For the Flavian heirs, the dispute involves both the contested history of a painting and the question of whether they were given a meaningful role in the agreement that enabled its sale. For Sotheby’s and Mondex, the central issues include the evidence supporting the looting allegation, the validity of the settlement and the court’s authority to hear the case.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy proposes seven transformative executive orders to be signed on his first day in office, targeting property tax reform, immigration cooperation, data center regulations, Medicaid efficiency, violent crime resolution, government spending oversight, and a new anti-fraud task force.
articles.body: Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy has announced seven executive orders he would sign on January 11 if elected, proposing changes to property tax oversight, immigration enforcement, data centre approvals, Medicaid spending and state government operations.“Here’s my list of Day 1 Executive Orders. They’ll be signed before midnight on January 11. Buckle up,” Ramaswamy wrote on X while sharing the proposals.One of the proposed orders would direct the Ohio Department of Taxation, in consultation with the Auditor of State, to review property tax increases across counties, townships, municipalities, school districts and special districts. Jurisdictions where property taxes have risen by more than 100% since 2020 would face a full investigation into how the additional revenue was spent and their financial requirements.Another proposal would restrict state funding for local governments that do not cooperate with federal immigration authorities. Under the plan, cities, townships and counties that fail to honour federal immigration detainer requests or share information as permitted by federal law could lose access to state grants, including public safety and homeland security funding. The policies could also be referred for legal action.Ramaswamy has also proposed pausing state agency action on applications, permits, incentives and approvals for new data centre projects until the Ohio General Assembly passes comprehensive legislation governing the sector.On healthcare spending, he wants the Department of Medicaid to seek a federal Section 1115 waiver to cap the state's Medicaid expenditure. The proposal draws on Tennessee's TennCare III model, under which the state could retain up to 55% of federal savings if spending remained below an agreed cap.Another order would direct the Departments of Public Safety and Rehabilitation and Corrections to prioritise violent crime clearance rates when allocating discretionary funding to local law enforcement. Ramaswamy's campaign puts Ohio's current clearance rate at 34% and says the proposal would support efforts to improve the number of violent crimes solved.He also wants a review of all executive-branch contracts funded through Ohio's General Revenue Fund. The Department of Administrative Services and the Office of Budget and Management would examine each contract's legal basis, necessity, performance and cost of termination before recommending whether it should continue.The seventh proposal would establish an inter-agency anti-fraud task force reporting directly to the governor. Its proposed areas of focus include Medicaid, benefits and childcare fraud, visa fraud, voter registration fraud, trucking violations, foreign commercial driver's licence issuance and the hiring of foreign workers by public entities.Ramaswamy is facing Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton in the Ohio governor's race. His campaign recently stopped airing an advertisement featuring Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, after it drew criticism from both Republicans and Democrats.Arthur appeared in the advertisement calling her daughter a "liar". Ramaswamy defended the campaign's decision, saying the advertisement focused on alleged dishonesty rather than Acton's childhood.
